Provenance: read from billing at 7133643d8eebb4dd5de2d8df34c7ba20fda89f79, from `Subscriptions::Lifecycle#payload/2` on the `customer.subscription.updated` path and from `core_payload/1`, which writes `email` and `plan_name` on every subscription payload. The commit is fleet.yml's sourceCommit for billing, and billing's tree was verifiably AT it (clean, HEAD) when this was transcribed. **RE-READ 2026-10-02 at that same commit, which is still billing's HEAD: this schema does not describe what its publisher emits.** The citation above is accurate about where the shape was looked for and wrong about the shape.

What billing emits, read out of `app/services/subscriptions/lifecycle.rb` at that commit. `payload/2` (line 350) is `core_payload(subscription).merge(detail_payload)` for this path, and neither half is what this file declares. `core_payload/1` (line 353) writes, unconditionally, `subscription_id` (billing's own `subscriptions.id`, a bare uuid), `plan_id` (`plans.id`, a bare uuid), `account_id` (`customers.owner_id`, identity's uuid), `status` and `currency`; then `quantity` only when the processor sent an Integer, and `trial_ends_at` only while `status == "trialing"`. `detail_payload` (line 368) adds `current_period_start`, `current_period_end`, `cancel_at_period_end`, `canceled_at`, `processor`, `processor_event_id` and `processor_subscription_id`. billing's own tests assert three of them — `plan_id`, `current_period_end` and `processor_event_id` at `test/services/subscriptions/lifecycle_test.rb:402-408, 368-372, 375-379` — and `PENDING_PAYLOAD_ALIGNMENT` at `test/contract/outbox_envelope_contract_test.rb:80-83` records the whole gap.

So this schema, closed with `additionalProperties: false`, **rejects five fields every real update carries** (`plan_id`, `account_id`, `currency`, `processor_subscription_id`, and `trial_ends_at` while trialing) and **requires two it never receives** (`kind`, `customer_id`). `processor` and `processor_event_id` ARE emitted on this path, by `detail_payload` rather than by `core_payload` — which is why they are not in billing's `missing` list. billing has said both halves in its own source: `lifecycle.rb:320-343` records that core's schemas "describe a different payload, and this is recorded rather than matched" and that "when core decides, the change lands here and in the contract test together".

**Why the transcription went stale rather than being wrong when written**, and what the packet that owns the fix has to weigh: D10 rewrote these three schemas because billing had no subscriptions table, true of billing-03b and false from `db/migrate/20260930000007_create_subscriptions.rb` onward. A payload schema describes what a publisher emits (docs/event-naming.md), so core owes this file a rewrite; D39 records why it is not in that commit and what flipping it costs. One asymmetry belongs in the record rather than in a schema's prose: `detail_payload` means the three types are **no longer one shape**, which this file's `description` also asserts. They were once, and the description is the surviving half of a claim that stopped being true.
title: billing.subscription.updated payload
description: The `data` payload of the `billing.subscription.updated` event: plan, quantity or interval changed. The payload is normalised from a payment processor's own webhook and is meant to have exactly the same shape as `billing.subscription.started` — same normaliser, same fields — so a consumer handles one reader, not two. It is the processor's current state and not a diff: `quantity` is the new number and `unit_amount` the new price, with nothing saying which of them moved. **Two claims in that paragraph have gone stale, and both are corrected in this file's `$comment` rather than here.** First: **this schema does not describe what its publisher emits, and the disagreement runs in both directions** — billing emits `plan_id`, `account_id`, `currency` and `processor_subscription_id`, which this closed schema refuses, and receives no `kind` and no `customer_id`, which it requires; the emitted key set, the source lines, the commit, and billing's own two-way record of the gap are all in the `$comment`. Second: the three subscription payloads are **no longer one shape** — billing's `detail_payload` adds the period, the cancellation intent, the processor's ids and its provenance to an update and a cancellation but not to a start, and that asymmetry is deliberate on billing's side. So the one-reader affordance this file offered no longer exists, and a consumer needs three. See [D39](../DECISIONS.md#d39-does-a-payload-schema-follow-its-publisher-when-the-publisher-has-grown-the-feature-the-schema-predicted-it-would-not). **The recipient fact and the plan's name, added 2026-10-07 (core-w46): `email` is OPTIONAL and NEVER NULL** — `core_payload` writes it only when `customer.email.present?` — **and `plan_name` is REQUIRED and non-empty**, written unconditionally from the plan row the builder has already resolved. Both are declared the way billing sends them. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

processor.description: The payment processor this subscription lives at.

processor_event_id.description: The processor's own event id for the webhook this came from, e.g. `evt_…`. Different on every update even when nothing material changed, so it is the deduplication key and not a version.

kind.description: Always `subscription`, as on every other subscription payload.

subscription_id.description: The processor's subscription id, e.g. `sub_…`. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`, and the same value every other event about this subscription carries.

customer_id.description: The processor's customer id, e.g. `cus_…`. Present on every update because it is what a consumer needs to attribute the change, and a subscription that changed without one would have no account to bill.

status.description: The subscription's status as the processor reports it. Not an enum in core: it is a third party's vocabulary. A change here is the one update a consumer must not treat as routine — it is how a subscription silently becomes `past_due`.

quantity.description: Units now billed for, or null when the subscription carries no quantity. The new number, not the delta.

price_id.description: The processor's price id, e.g. `price_…`, or null. A change here is a plan change, which is the event's main subject.

unit_amount.description: Price per unit now, as integer minor units and a currency — or null when the processor sent neither.

amount_minor.description: Per-unit amount in the currency's minor units. The new amount, not the delta.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, uppercase, normalised on the way in.

current_period_start.description: RFC3339 UTC when the current billing period began, or null. A mid-period plan change does not move this, which is why `unit_amount` and this disagree after an update and are not redundant.

current_period_end.description: RFC3339 UTC when the current billing period ends.

cancel_at_period_end.description: Whether the subscription is set to stop at the end of the period. False is not null: false is a decision, null is the absence of one.

canceled_at.description: RFC3339 UTC when the subscription was cancelled, or null while it has not been.

trial.description: Whether the subscription has a trial. The publisher derives this, so it is never null.

email.description: The customer's billing email, or ABSENT — never null — when there is no address to carry. `core_payload` writes it only when `customer.email.present?`: a customer created in the processor's dashboard has no anywaye row, and one created through `/v1` has no email until the client sets one. Optional and non-nullable for that reason: required would reject every event for a customer with no address, and nullable would promise a shape billing never sends. Named `email` to match identity's events, which carry the same fact for the same reason — one fleet, one field name for the address a consumer cannot look up.

plan_name.description: The plan's own name beside its id. `core_payload` writes it unconditionally from the plan row the builder has already resolved, so it costs no query the payload was not already making — the same reason `currency` is here. Required and non-empty: `plans.name` is `null: false` with a presence validation, so a blank name is not a state the publisher can be in. A mail about a subscription change has to say which plan, and `plan_id` is a uuid no consumer can render into words.
